bihar_raw_news.title: 'Major achievement for entire Kosi region': Bihar CM after AAI floats tender for Saharsa ... - DD India
bihar_raw_news.content: What's New Share DD India September 10, 2026 11:29 AM IST Airports Authority of India (AAI) | Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary | Major achievement for entire Kosi region | Saharsa Airport upgrade ‘Major achievement for entire Kosi region’: Bihar CM after AAI floats tender for Saharsa Airport upgrade Author: DD India Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday said the Airports Authority of India (AAI) has floated a tender worth Rs 42.52 crore for the development and upgradation of Saharsa Airport, describing it as a major step towards improving air connectivity in the Kosi region. Sharing the development on X, Choudhary thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said the project would strengthen air connectivity to Saharsa and adjoining areas. “Historic step towards providing air connectivity to Saharsa! Gratitude to the country’s illustrious Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji. The AAI has published a tender of ₹42.52 crore for the development and upgradation of Saharsa Airport. This is a major achievement for the entire Kosi region,” he said. The chief minister said the state government was providing 12 acres of land for the project at an estimated cost of Rs 147 crore. “12 acres of land is being provided by the state government at a cost of ₹147 crore. This will pave the way for swift air connectivity to the entire Kosi region, including Saharsa,” Choudhary said. The airport’s development is expected to improve accessibility for residents of the region and provide a new transportation link that could support trade and tourism. Meanwhile, Choudhary on Wednesday felicitated 168 meritorious students who secured positions in the topper lists of the 2026 Intermediate and Matriculation annual examinations at a ceremony held at the ‘Nek Samvad’ auditorium of Lok Sevak Awas in Patna. The students were presented medals, certificates and cash awards for their academic achievements. Those securing the first position received Rs 2 lakh, while second and third rank holders were awarded Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 1 lakh, respectively. Intermediate students securing fourth and fifth positions received Rs 30,000 each, while Matriculation students ranked fourth to tenth were awarded Rs 20,000 each. All 168 students were also provided Rs 51,000 each to purchase laptops. Addressing the students, Choudhary said the meritorious students represented Bihar’s bright future and would make an important contribution to the state’s development. (ANI Inputs)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Govt revises honorarium for contractual faculty, resident doctors - Medical Dialogues
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Govt revises honorarium for contractual faculty, resident doctors Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Rumela De Sarkar Published On 2026-09-10 05:25 GMT | Update On 2026-09-10 05:25 GMT Patna: State-run medical colleges and hospitals in Bihar will now pay higher monthly honoraria to contractual professors, associate professors, assistant professors, and resident doctors, following a state government's decision to revise their remuneration. According to an order issued by the health department , the monthly honorarium for contractual professors has been increased from Rs 1.80 lakh to Rs 2.07 lakh. Contractual associate professors will now receive Rs 1.55 lakh, up from Rs 1.35 lakh, while the honorarium for assistant professors has been raised from Rs 1.10 lakh to Rs 1.25 lakh, reports The Daily. Also Read:Doctors oppose Bihar govt's ban on private practice The government has also revised the monthly honorarium for senior residents and tutors to Rs 1.15 lakh. The honorarium for junior residents has been increased from Rs 65,000 to Rs 75,000. The revised rates will be effective retrospectively from September 1, 2026, the health department said. The proposal was approved following recommendations of the authorised committee and approval from the competent authority. The department has directed the concerned medical colleges and hospitals to implement the revised honorarium rates. Speaking to TOI, Health Minister Nishant Kumar said the govt was taking measures to strengthen the healthcare and medical education system. “Contractual professors, associate professors, assistant professors, senior residents and junior residents play an important role in the functioning of govt medical colleges. Keeping in view their contributions, the govt has decided to increase their honorarium,” Nishant said. He added that the decision would provide an incentive to medical professionals and strengthen the availability of specialised and qualified human resources at government medical colleges. The health department said the increase was intended to support the functioning of state-run medical colleges and hospitals by helping attract and retain qualified contractual faculty and resident doctors. Medical Dialogues had previously reported that critically injured patients at Patna Medical College and Hospital (PMCH) could soon receive coordinated trauma care within 15 minutes of arrival, with the hospital preparing a proposal to establish a Level-1 trauma centre. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar ₹1,100 pension: do e-KYC now or the money stops
bihar_raw_news.content: Schemes Bihar ₹1,100 pension: do e-KYC now or the money stops Bihar has raised its old-age, widow and disability pensions to ₹1,100 a month — more than double the old ₹400 — and paid over 97 lakh people. But the money now lands only if the pensioner's e-KYC is done and the bank account is Aadhaar-seeded. Skip it and the next instalment is quietly held. Here's exactly what to do, for free, so a parent's pension keeps coming. Dr. Rakesh Choudhary • Published 10 September 2026 • Editorial policy हिंदी में पढ़ें Schemes A son helps his elderly mother complete pension e-KYC on a phone outside their Bihar village home. View as Web Story View the official notification Bihar Department of Social Welfare — Social Security Pension Management Information System (SSPMIS, sspmis.bihar.gov.in) and the e-Labharthi payment portal (elabharthi.bih.nic.in). Pension raised to ₹1,100/month across old-age (Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojana), widow (Laxmibai Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana) and disability schemes (a ₹700 increase over the earlier ₹400), confirmed by Prabhat Khabar and other outlets (97.84 lakh beneficiaries, ~₹1,424 crore released). e-KYC and Aadhaar-seeded (DBT/NPCI-mapped) bank account mandatory for payment per SSPMIS/e-Labharthi. Verify the current process and any state deadline on sspmis.bihar.gov.in before acting. Advertisement If your mother or father in Bihar gets a state pension, this is the one small job worth doing this month — before the money stops. Bihar has made its social security pension much bigger. The old-age, widow and disability pensions have been raised to ₹1,100 a month — up from the old ₹400 — and in the latest round more than 97 lakh people were paid. That is a real, useful jump for a household that runs on it. But there is a catch that trips up thousands of families every cycle: the higher pension only reaches the account if the beneficiary’s e-KYC is done and the bank account is Aadhaar-seeded . Skip that, and the next instalment is simply held. Nobody sends a warning letter. The family usually finds out when the money doesn’t arrive. What actually changed, and who gets ₹1,100 The state runs three main pensions through the same system. All three now pay the same higher amount. Pension Who it is for Now pays Old-age (Vridhjan) Senior citizens (broadly 60+) ₹1,100 / month Widow (Laxmibai) Eligible widows ₹1,100 / month Disability (Viklang) Persons with disability ₹1,100 / month The money is paid straight into the beneficiary’s bank account by Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). No middleman, no queue at an office to collect cash — which is exactly why the account details have to be perfect. Why a running pension suddenly stops e-KYC is now compulsory. When a beneficiary’s verification is pending or fails, the department holds that person’s payment instead of releasing it. This is not a cut — it is a pause until the identity is confirmed again. national_raw_news.title: 42 mins ago | National 38 India calls on BRICS countries to expand opportunities for women-led enterprises in global trade
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has called on BRICS countries to work together to expand opportunities for women entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises in international trade. Addressing the BRICS WBA Women-Led Development Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal stressed the need for easier access to credit and markets, along with predictable business rules. The Commerce Minister said India is focused on empowering women through financial inclusion, education, skills and improved quality of life, with the aim of making them drivers of the country’s growth. He noted that nearly 300 million women in India have bank accounts, while collateral-free loans are provided to women seeking to start their own work, including those without a credit history. Mr Goyal also said around 100 million rural women are members of over nine million self-help groups under the ‘Lakhpati Didis’ initiative, aimed at ensuring women’s economic independence and greater contribution to India’s growth. Mr Goyal also urged governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to participate more actively in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions and business forums. Calling for greater engagement among BRICS countries, the minister said dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward towards a more prosperous future for member countries, partner countries and the world. He also highlighted that India has set a target of growing from a four trillion dollar economy today to a thirty trillion dollar economy by 2047, when the country celebrates 100 years of Independence.

national_raw_news.title: 42 mins ago | National 29 India ramps up Nepal flood relief with 8th aid flight, specialised tunnel team and forensic experts
national_raw_news.content: India has intensified its humanitarian assistance to Nepal in the wake of devastating flash floods, delivering over 130 tonnes of relief material and deploying 54 expert personnel to support search, rescue, and forensic operations. The Indian Embassy in Nepal said yesterday that an eighth Indian Air Force aircraft carrying 35 tonnes of relief and rescue supplies landed in Kathmandu, marking the latest shipment in a continuous aid effort launched on August 26, 2026. India has also dispatched specialised technical gear, including mud rescue suits, gas detectors, breathing apparatus, inflatable walkways, portable generators, lighting towers, and dewatering pumps. India has provided DNA kits, reagents, and equipment for DNA profiling to aid in victim identification. Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs also noted the handing over of the relief aid by Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava to Nepal’s Minister Mahabir Pun upon the arrival of the eighth aircraft. Meanwhile, India’s specialised tunnel rescue team initially launched joint operations with the Nepali Army across two high-risk sites in Chilime and Langtang. Search efforts are currently concentrated at the Chilime tunnel, where rescue workers face severe operational hurdles due to rugged terrain, constrained access, and steep tunnel inclines. Teams are currently constructing a makeshift access path to transport heavy machinery, such as excavators, directly to the tunnel entrance. Construction on the track is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed within two to three days.
